relations.definition: To be utilized or employed by someone or something.
relations.embedding_query_text: used by: To be utilized or employed by someone or something.

chosen_property.label: utilizedBy
chosen_property.definition: To be utilized or employed by someone or something.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: skills
candidates.comment: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

relations.definition: To reduce the amount of time required for someone or something to complete a task.
relations.embedding_query_text: saves time for: To reduce the amount of time required for someone or something to complete a task.

chosen_property.label: savesTimeFor
chosen_property.definition: To reduce the amount of time required for someone or something to complete a task.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: performTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to execute instructions or a direction, excluding preparation time. Also called execution time, active time, task duration. Examples: A recipe's instructions have a perform time of 'PT30M'. A DIY project direction has a perform time of 'PT2H'. A workout routine has a perform time of 'PT45M'. Distinct from prepTime, which is the time to prepare supplies.

candidates.label: totalTime
candidates.comment: A total time relation between instructions or a direction and the overall duration required to perform them, including preparation. Also called overall duration, completion time, estimated time. Examples: "HowTo totalTime 'PT2H30M'", "HowToDirection totalTime 'PT15M'", "Recipe totalTime 'PT1H'".

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: timeToComplete
candidates.comment: A duration representing the expected length of time to complete an educational or occupational program when attending full-time. Also called "program duration", "completion duration", "full-time study length", "expected completion time". Examples: "The degree program has timeToComplete 4 years", "The certification's timeToComplete is 6 months", "This program requires timeToComplete 2 years of full-time study."

candidates.label: prepTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to prepare items for use in instructions or a direction. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe has a prep time of 'PT15M'. A DIY project has a prep time of 'PT30M'. A cooking instruction has a prep time of 'PT10M'. Distinct from performTime, which is the time to execute the instructions.

candidates.label: handlingTime
candidates.comment: A processing time relation between a shipping service or delivery time and the duration required for order fulfillment. Also called processing duration, preparation time, fulfillment time, lead time. Examples: "A shipping service has a handling time of 2 days.", "The delivery time includes a handling time of 1-3 business days.", "Order processing has a handling time of 24 hours."

candidates.label: processingTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the estimated duration required to process a service request through a specific channel. Also called handling time, turnaround time, service duration. Examples: A service channel has a processing time of 'PT2H'. The online application has a processing time of 'P3D'. The customer support channel has a processing time of 'PT15M'.

candidates.label: cookTime
candidates.comment: A temporal measurement for a recipe, indicating the duration required to cook the dish. Also called "cooking duration", "preparation time", "time to cook". Examples: "Recipe 'Chicken Curry' cookTime 'PT30M'", "Recipe 'Cake' cookTime 'PT45M'". Distinct from prepTime, which is the time for preparation before cooking, and totalTime, which is the sum of all time.

candidates.label: activityDuration
candidates.comment: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."

candidates.label: endTime
candidates.comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". Distinct from endDate, which specifies the end date for longer-term items like events or seasons.

relations.definition: To gather data or information through a systematic process of questioning or observation.
relations.embedding_query_text: conducted survey: To gather data or information through a systematic process of questioning or observation.

instances: U.S. Census Bureau -> Census Bureau survey

chosen_property.label: conductedSurvey
chosen_property.definition: To gather data or information through a systematic process of questioning or observation.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: measurementTechnique
candidates.comment: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.

candidates.label: measurementMethod
candidates.comment: A measurement method relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the specific method used for measurement. Also called: method of measurement, specific technique, measurement approach. Examples: "Temperature Dataset measurementMethod 'Thermocouple'", "Survey Data measurementMethod 'Likert Scale'", "Chemical Analysis measurementMethod 'Spectrophotometry'". Distinct from measurementTechnique, which is a broader property that measurementMethod is a subproperty of.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: measuredProperty
candidates.comment: A measured property relation between an observation or statistical variable and the property being measured. Also called: property measured, observed characteristic, variable property. Examples: "Temperature Observation measuredProperty 'temperature'", "GDP StatisticalVariable measuredProperty 'Gross Domestic Product'", "Survey Response measuredProperty 'satisfaction level'". Distinct from variableMeasured, which is a broader property for describing what is measured in a dataset.

candidates.label: studyDesign
candidates.comment: A specification of the design methodology for a medical observational study. Also called "observational study type", "research design", "study methodology". Examples: "The study has studyDesign CohortStudy", "The medical observational study's studyDesign is CrossSectionalStudy", "This research uses a studyDesign of CaseControlStudy."

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: measurementQualifier
candidates.comment: A measurement qualifier relation between an observation or statistical variable and an enumeration providing additional qualification. Also called: observation qualifier, measurement attribute, data context. Examples: "GDP Observation measurementQualifier 'Nominal'", "Inflation Rate measurementQualifier 'Annualized'", "Population Count measurementQualifier 'Estimated'".

relations.definition: To discover or determine something through investigation or research.
relations.embedding_query_text: found that: To discover or determine something through investigation or research.

instances: Census Bureau survey -> AI saves workers time

chosen_property.label: discovered
chosen_property.definition: To find or learn about someone or something for the first time.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: identifyingTest
candidates.comment: An identifying test relation between a medical sign and a medical test that can detect it. Also called diagnostic test, detection test, test for sign. Examples: "A medical sign has an identifying test of a blood panel.", "The symptom is detected by an identifying test.", "This sign requires an identifying test.". Distinct from identifyingExam, which refers to a physical examination.

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: catalog
candidates.comment: A containment relation between a dataset and the data catalog that holds it. Also called "contained in catalog", "part of catalog", "dataset catalog". Examples: "Census data dataset catalog National Data Archive", "Research dataset catalog University Data Repository".

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

relations.definition: To investigate or study a particular topic or subject.
relations.embedding_query_text: conducted research on: To investigate or study a particular topic or subject.

instances: Massachusetts Institute of Technology -> MIT research on AI adoption

chosen_property.label: researched
chosen_property.definition: To investigate or study a particular topic or subject.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

candidates.label: specialty
candidates.comment: A categorization of a webpage's content by its domain specialty. Also called "domain expertise", "content area", "subject specialty", "field of study". Examples: "This medical webpage has specialty Cardiology", "The research paper's specialty is Artificial Intelligence", "The blog post's specialty is Vegan Cooking."

candidates.label: studyDesign

Examples: "The study has studyDesign CohortStudy", "The medical observational study's studyDesign is CrossSectionalStudy", "This research uses a studyDesign of CaseControlStudy."

candidates.label: guidelineSubject
candidates.comment: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline subject "Hypertension", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline subject "Type 2 Diabetes", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline subject "COVID-19". Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: observationAbout

relations.definition: To apply or utilize a theoretical or conceptual framework to understand or explain a phenomenon.
relations.embedding_query_text: use model: To apply or utilize a theoretical or conceptual framework to understand or explain a phenomenon.

chosen_property.label: utilizesModel
chosen_property.definition: To apply or utilize a theoretical or conceptual framework to understand or explain a phenomenon.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: model
candidates.comment: A model relation between a product and its product model or textual identifier. Also called: product model, version, type. Examples: "Smartphone model 'iPhone 15 Pro'", "Car model 'Toyota Camry'", "Laptop model 'MacBook Air M2'".

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: educationalFramework
candidates.comment: An educational framework relation between an alignment object and the text describing the framework to which a resource is aligned. Also called "alignment framework", "standard framework", "curriculum standard". Examples: "Alignment object educationalFramework 'Common Core State Standards'", "Alignment object educationalFramework 'Next Generation Science Standards'", "Alignment object educationalFramework 'European Qualifications Framework'". Distinct from educationalAlignment, which links a resource to an alignment object.

candidates.label: isResizable
candidates.comment: A model property relation indicating whether a 3D model can be scaled or resized. Also called resizable, scalable, adjustable size. Examples: A 3D model of a chair has isResizable set to 'true'. A 3D model of a building has isResizable set to 'false'. A 3D model of a character has isResizable set to 'true'.

candidates.label: programmingModel
candidates.comment: A programming model relation between an API reference and its management paradigm (managed or unmanaged). Also called API model, management type. Examples: "A .NET API has a programming model 'managed'.", "A C++ library API has a programming model 'unmanaged'.", "A Java API has a programming model 'managed'."

candidates.label: modelDate
candidates.comment: A model date relation between a vehicle and the release date of its model. Also called: model year, release date, version date. Examples: "Car modelDate 2023-09-01", "Motorcycle modelDate 2024-01-15", "Truck modelDate 2022-07-01".

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: diagram
candidates.comment: An illustrative relation between an anatomical structure and an image containing a diagram of it. Also called: anatomical illustration, structural diagram, visual representation. Examples: "Human Heart" diagram "Image of heart chambers and vessels", "Brain Anatomy" diagram "Diagram showing lobes and functions", "Skeletal System" diagram "Illustration of bone structure".

candidates.label: isVariantOf
candidates.comment: A product variation relation between a product or product model and the base product or product group from which it is a specific variant. Also called variant of, version of, derived from product, specific model of. Examples: A 'red iPhone 15' isVariantOf 'iPhone 15 Pro'. A 'size L t-shirt' isVariantOf 'Basic T-Shirt ProductGroup'. A 'diesel car model' isVariantOf 'Car Model X'. Distinct from isRelatedTo or isSimilarTo, as it implies a direct hierarchical relationship of variation from a base product or group.

chosen_property.label: assists
chosen_property.definition: To provide assistance or support to someone or something.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: softwareHelp
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."

candidates.label: productSupported
candidates.comment: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."

candidates.label: distinguishingSign
candidates.comment: A distinguishing sign relation between a differential diagnosis element and a medical sign or symptom that helps differentiate it from other diagnoses. Also called "differential symptom", "diagnostic indicator", "key symptom". Examples: "DDx element 'Appendicitis' distinguishingSign 'Right lower quadrant pain'", "DDx element 'Flu' distinguishingSign 'Sudden onset'", "DDx element 'Migraine' distinguishingSign 'Aura'".

candidates.label: physiologicalBenefits
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the specific physiological benefits associated with a diet plan. Also called health advantages, bodily benefits, wellness effects. Examples: A diet has physiological benefits like 'improved cardiovascular health'. A diet has physiological benefits like 'weight loss'. A diet has physiological benefits like 'reduced inflammation'.

candidates.label: inSupportOf
candidates.comment: A support relation between a thesis and the qualification, candidature, degree, or application it supports. Also called supports for, for the purpose of, in aid of. Examples: "A thesis is in support of a PhD degree.", "The research is in support of a qualification.", "This thesis is written in support of an application."

candidates.label: possibleTreatment
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.

candidates.label: providesService
candidates.comment: A service provision relation between a service channel and the specific service it delivers. Also called channel delivers, service offered via, offers service. Examples: "An online portal provides service 'customer support'.", "A phone line provides service 'technical assistance'.", "A mobile app provides service 'online banking'."

candidates.label: benefits
candidates.comment: A description of benefits associated with a job posting. Also called: job perks, employee benefits, compensation package details. Examples: "JobPosting 'Marketing Manager' benefits 'Health insurance, 401k, paid time off'", "JobPosting 'Developer' benefits 'Flexible hours, remote work option'."

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: supplyTo
candidates.comment: An anatomical supply relation between an artery and the anatomical structure to which it provides blood. Also called "feeds blood to", "irrigates", "provides blood for", "vascularizes". Examples: "The carotid artery suppliesTo the brain", "The femoral artery suppliesTo the leg", "This artery suppliesTo various tissues."

chosen_property.label: reducesTimeFor

chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: cutoffTime

Also called: order cutoff, daily processing limit, last order time. Examples: "Same-day Delivery" cutoff time "14:00:00-05:00", "Next-day Shipping" cutoff time "17:00:00Z", "Warehouse Processing" cutoff time "23:30:00-05:00".

candidates.label: deliveryLeadTime
candidates.comment: A temporal delay relation between a demand or offer and the typical time between order receipt and goods leaving the warehouse or being ready for pickup. Also called: lead time, dispatch time, preparation time. Examples: "Product Offer" delivery lead time "2-3 business days", "Custom Order" delivery lead time "1 week", "In-store Pickup" delivery lead time "2 hours". Distinct from deliveryTime, which is the total time until the goods reach the customer.

candidates.label: endTime
candidates.comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". Distinct from endDate, which specifies the end date for longer-term items like events or seasons.

candidates.label: deliveryTime
candidates.comment: A temporal duration relation between delivery time settings or offer shipping details and the total delay from order receipt to goods reaching the final customer. Also called: total delivery time, shipping duration, estimated delivery. Examples: "Standard Shipping" delivery time "5-7 business days", "Express Delivery" delivery time "1-2 days", "International Shipment" delivery time "2-3 weeks". Distinct from deliveryLeadTime, which is the time until dispatch or pickup readiness.

candidates.label: availableThrough

Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableThrough '2023-10-30T17:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableThrough '2023-11-01'". Distinct from availableFrom, which specifies the start of pickup availability.

candidates.label: closes
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for opening hours, indicating the closing time for a place or service on a given day. Also called "closing time", "end of hours", "closes at". Examples: "Store opening hours closes '18:00'", "Service opening hours closes '22:30'". Distinct from opens, which specifies the opening time.

candidates.label: cookTime
candidates.comment: A temporal measurement for a recipe, indicating the duration required to cook the dish. Also called "cooking duration", "preparation time", "time to cook". Examples: "Recipe 'Chicken Curry' cookTime 'PT30M'", "Recipe 'Cake' cookTime 'PT45M'". Distinct from prepTime, which is the time for preparation before cooking, and totalTime, which is the sum of all time.

candidates.label: restPeriods
candidates.comment: A specification of the recommended breaks or recovery times within an exercise plan. Also called break times, recovery intervals, downtime. Examples: `HIIT Workout Plan` restPeriods `"30 seconds between sets"`, `Marathon Training Schedule` restPeriods `"One rest day per week"`, `Weightlifting Routine` restPeriods `"90 seconds between exercises"`.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: prepTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to prepare items for use in instructions or a direction. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe has a prep time of 'PT15M'. A DIY project has a prep time of 'PT30M'. A cooking instruction has a prep time of 'PT10M'. Distinct from performTime, which is the time to execute the instructions.
